key_insight: The paper shows that many common similarity assumptions are too weak to close the optimization-time gap between homogeneous and heterogeneous asynchronous training, and identifies a stronger minimal assumption pair that does.
engineering_relevance: For distributed ML systems, this clarifies when asynchronous training can achieve homogeneous-style speedups and when heterogeneity fundamentally limits wall-clock performance.
method: Proves impossibility results under first- and second-order similarity assumptions for randomized algorithms
Tests the interpolation regime and shows weak interpolation alone still cannot close the gap
Introduces strong interpolation plus a local Polyak–Lojasiewicz condition to obtain a sharper time-complexity bound
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical analysis and complexity bounds rather than experiments, using comparison to known optimal results in homogeneous and heterogeneous settings.
watch_item: The new guarantee depends on stronger structural assumptions, so its practical applicability may be limited if real worker data are only weakly aligned.
paper_title: Bridging the Gap Between Homogeneous and Heterogeneous Asynchronous Optimization Is Surprisingly Difficult
